subject: 062 navigation rail — narrow overlay keyboard containment defect, reproduced and fixed
finding: ACCEPTED: at 360 with the narrow overlay open, Tab off the last destination left the document (body) and then landed on #proto-toggle behind #nav-scrim; Shift+Tab off the toggle reached #compare-open and #proto-toggle the same way. syncNav() made .shell-bar, #work-region, #dock-region and #status inert but omitted #proto-bar, and the keydown handler had no Tab/Shift+Tab containment.
fix: syncNav() now toggles inert on #proto-bar with the other covered regions, so every route that closes the menu (Close control, Escape, dimmer, destination, breakpoint crossing) restores the whole background through the same line. The existing document keydown handler now wraps Tab/Shift+Tab across the visible enabled rail controls (navStops()) while state.navExpanded && navIsOverlay(), and pulls focus back if it has drifted outside. The wide inline pane is untouched and keeps the ordinary tab order.

focusCapture.method: overlay opened with native Enter (text "\r"), then two native Shift+Tab presses from the named toggle

environmentNotes: Edge marks the headless target visibilityState "hidden" after this focus sequence (the r6 report saw the same); a hidden page receives no resize or media-query change events, so every breakpoint observation calls Page.bringToFront and confirms document.visibilityState before reading the frame.
Breakpoint steps wait for the real innerWidth, the real media-query state and an actual change event on a passive observer. No synthetic change or resize event was dispatched.
